title: The Opera House

q: Pin your plan on the wall.

cards.sub: MORE TASKS? MORE PADDING? ANOTHER WALL?
12 MONTHS: 3 IN 10 · ASK HOW THE LAST THOUSAND WENT

captions: Five people signed this schedule. Nothing is missing.
Task one: discovery. One month, if all goes well.
Design, build, test, launch. Each one, if all goes well.
Add it up: 12 months. Every task has a reason.
The plan says 12. When will it really be done?
Pause and choose a month. Hold it.
Sealed. The case opens it later.
1959. Sydney plans an opera house: four years, $7 million.
Opened 1973. Fourteen years. $102 million.
Three and a half times the time. Fourteen times the money.
Keep your month, or change it.
A thousand projects like yours. One bar each, as long as it took.
Sort them. Three hundred finished on their plan.
Is your project more like the 300, or the 700?
Your plan is twelve months. Lay it on the wall.
Three hundred of a thousand finished by month twelve.
Twelve months: three in ten. Seven in ten run past it.
Most of us write down the plan. The wall says: half need 15½.
To be eight-in-ten sure, say 23. Nearly double.
12 is a hope. 15½ is the middle. 23 is a promise.
A team writing a textbook. Everyone's estimate: about two years.
He knew the wall: seven to ten years. Four in ten never finished.
They kept going anyway. It took eight years.
A plan is a story about us. A wall is a count of them.
Add three tasks. The plan is 15. On the wall: still 3 in 10.
Promise 24 instead: eight in ten projects finished by then.
A different count: 8.5 % hit time and budget.
Detail does not move you on the wall. Only the wall does.
Task by task is the inside view. The wall is the outside view.
Ask: what is this a case of? Where on that wall are we?
Five people signed twelve months. The wall said three in ten.
rev: REV E · ON THE WALL · 3 IN 10
REV F · A STORY, NOT A COUNT
REV G · MORE TASKS: SAME ODDS
